frequency_question: What proportion of major partisan voting reform bills that achieve significant legislative momentum ultimately pass the Senate in identical or successor form before the expiration of the congressional session?
membership_rule: Members are major federal voting reform bills introduced with party leadership backing that reach floor consideration or serious committee markup; excluded are trivial non-starter bills introduced purely for symbolic purposes without leadership backing.
coverage_note: 5 major instances identified spanning 1993 to present, capturing both bipartisan compromises and partisan stalemates.
known_gaps: Some minor committee-level amendments or unrecorded procedural votes omitted.
skeleton: Total major partisan voting bills considered by Senate divided by those successfully passing
multiplier: 2 hits out of 5 major identifiable partisan election reform pushes since 1993
validity_reason: Senate rules regarding the filibuster and cloture remain stable over this multi-decade baseline horizon.
